origin.note: A collection of accounts classifying posted transactions by account.

theory.definition: The general ledger organizes posted transactions into individual accounts.
theory.purpose: It accumulates balances for checking and financial reporting.
principles: Every posting is linked to a source record.
Debits and credits retain their double-entry relationship.
rules: Transfer each journal line to the named account.
Keep debit and credit sides distinct.
Balance or carry forward accounts according to the reporting period.

posting_steps: Use balances in the trial balance.

exercise.prompt: Post journal entries to the relevant T-accounts.
exercise.answer_rule: Each transaction must appear on both corresponding ledger accounts.

on_statements: Provides balances used in the trial balance and statements.
on_decisions: Inspect individual account activity and balances.
risk_if_wrong: Incomplete postings lead to incomplete account balances.

depth.level_1: Accounts group transaction postings by category.
depth.level_2: Post each journal line, maintain both sides, and calculate the account balance.
depth.level_3: Subsidiary ledgers may support control accounts; compare account-by-account detail to the chronological journal.
